per_case.output: Ama mala is characterized by symptoms such as lethargy, indigestion, poor appetite, bad breath, coated tongue, foul body odor, sticky stools, and generalized heaviness. These arise because undigested food particles mix with waste products, creating toxic byproducts that impair bodily functions. In contrast, nirama mala typically presents without these systemic disturbances; digestion is complete, and elimination occurs smoothly. The presence of ama in excreta often necessitates prior use of dipana (appetizers) and pachana (digestants) before any purification procedures. This distinction is crucial for determining appropriate therapeutic sequencing in clinical practice.

The following symptoms indicate sama doshas: a feeling of fullness, lack of appetite, nausea, excessive salivation, body ache, lethargy, drowsiness, malaise, anorexia, tastelessness, and mental fogginess. These arise due to undigested food particles mixing with vitiated doshas, impairing digestion and causing systemic toxicity. The presence of these signs confirms ama formation and necessitates langhana (lightening) therapies before any pacification measures can be effective.

साम मल के लक्षण इस प्रकार हैं - अपच की अनुभूति, आमाशय में भारीपन, अजीर्णता, शरीर में ग्लानि, जी मिचलाना, थकान, त्वचा पर दाह, नाड़ी में मंदता, जिह्वा पर श्वेत शिरा आदि। जबकि निराम मल के लक्षण ये हैं - स्पष्ट रंग, सुगंधित गंध, नियमित समय पर त्याग, बिना असुविधा के निकलना, हल्कापन महसूस होना, भूख लगना, स्वस्थ पाचन संकेत। यह विवरण चरक सूत्रस्थान 16 एवं कार्श्यप संहिता सूत्रस्थान 7 में वर्णित है।

The texts describe sama vata as having symptoms similar to normal vata but without its typical aggravation patterns such as pain on movement. It is balanced and functions normally. Sama pitta is described as being free from excess heat and inflammation, maintaining healthy digestion and metabolism. Sama kapha refers to a state where kapha dosha is neither increased nor decreased, providing stability, moisture, and strength. These states represent equilibrium among all three doshas.

When doshas are called "sama," they refer to a state where ama is present due to impaired agni. This condition makes the doshas heavy, sticky, and difficult to eliminate. The term indicates that the disease process has progressed beyond simple aggravation into a more complex stage involving metabolic toxicity. Sama doshas require initial treatment focused on digesting ama before any pacification or elimination therapies can be effective.

साम वात के लक्षण इस प्रकार हैं: आध्मान (पेट फूलना), अरुचि (भूख न लगना), गौरव (शरीर में भारीपन), शीतज्वर (ठंड की अनुभूति), और मलिन मूत्र-पुरीष। ये सभी लक्षण आम के साथ दोषों के संयोग के कारण उत्पन्न होते हैं।

Food must be taken in proper quantity because overeating causes indigestion and ama formation while undereating leads to weakness and tissue depletion. The ideal matra is determined by one’s digestive capacity (agni), constitution (prakriti), season, age, and activity level. It ensures optimal nourishment without burdening digestion. This principle maintains dosha balance and prevents disease onset. Proper matra also allows space for vata movement and metabolic processes. Hence, individualized assessment is key rather than a fixed standard.

In sufficient quantities, food fuels the digestive fire and allows it to function properly. When eaten in moderation, food maintains balanced digestion and prevents the formation of ama. Eating too much overwhelms the digestive system, weakening agni and leading to indigestion and toxin accumulation. Conversely, eating too little fails to provide enough fuel for the digestive process, resulting in irregular agni activity. Thus, finding the right balance ensures optimal metabolic health and overall well-being.

आयुर्वेद में कहा गया है कि भोजन की मात्रा व्यक्ति की पाचन शक्ति पर निर्भर करती है — जिसे जठराग्नि कहते हैं। जो लोग अधिक खाते हैं लेकिन पचा नहीं पाते, उनमें आम बनता है, जो रोगों का मूल कारण है। इसलिए, प्रत्येक व्यक्ति की अपनी विशिष्ट अग्नि होती है जिसके अनुसार उसे कितना और कब खाना चाहिए।

INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE. The provided references do not address the measurement of food. They discuss appropriate quantity of medicines and dietary regimens based on individual constitution and digestive capacity rather than specific measurements for food intake.

When food is consumed in a sufficient quantity, all six tastes and qualities are present and balanced, leading to proper nourishment of the body tissues and optimal function of Agni. This results in satisfaction after eating, absence of discomfort, and regular elimination of waste products. In contrast, insufficient food intake fails to provide adequate nutrition, weakening the Dhatus and impairing their functions. Excessive food consumption overwhelms the digestive capacity, resulting in incomplete digestion and formation of Ama, which can clog bodily channels and lead to various diseases. Thus, both deficiency and excess disrupt the equilibrium of Doshas and contribute to disease onset.
कम मात्रा में खाने पर अग्नि प्रदीप्त होती है और पाचन ठीक रहता है। लेकिन अधिक मात्रा में खाने पर अग्नि मंद पड़ जाती है और आम बन जाता है। इसलिए संतुलित आहार ही स्वास्थ्य के लिए आवश्यक है।

Dandalasaka refers to a severe form of diarrhea caused by consuming contaminated water during travel, leading to rapid deterioration due to toxin exposure. It involves vitiation of all three doshas—Vata causes pain and distension, Pitta leads to burning sensation and fever, Kapha contributes to mucus and heaviness. The condition can quickly lead to dehydration, weakness, and even death if untreated. Hence, it must be strictly avoided through proper purification of drinking water and adherence to dietary rules while traveling.

Amavisha refers to a toxic state caused by incomplete digestion leading to the formation of ama—undigested food particles that circulate in the body and deposit in tissues. It is particularly dangerous because it can trigger chronic inflammatory conditions, autoimmune reactions, and systemic toxicity. Unlike simple ama, which results from weak agni, amavisha arises when ama undergoes qualitative change due to prolonged accumulation and interaction with doshas. This transformation makes it more reactive and difficult to eliminate. The concept underscores the importance of addressing digestive health as a foundational aspect of preventing disease.
आमविष अपचित आहारजनित विषैला पदार्थ है जो अग्नि की कमजोरी और दोष विकृति के कारण बनता है। यह शरीर में विभिन्न रोगों का मूल कारण माना जाता है।

No. Pain relief is contraindicated because it may suppress symptoms without resolving underlying digestive issues and can lead to complications such as ama accumulation and dosha vitiation. Proper management involves addressing agnimandya through dietary correction and light digestion-promoting herbs before considering analgesic measures if needed.

The statement "agni overwhelmed by āma cannot digest medicine and food" is based on the principle that impaired digestion prevents proper metabolism of both nutrients and medicines. When jāṭharāgni is weak due to āma formation from undigested food, even therapeutic substances may become toxic (viruddha ahāra). This leads to further vitiation of doshas instead of pacifying them. Additionally, āma blocks srotas (channels), preventing effective delivery and action of drugs. Hence, administering medicine without first correcting agni risks aggravating disease rather than curing it.

In other words, if the digestive fire is too weak to process food, it's equally incapable of processing potent herbs or formulations. This concept underscores the Ayurvedic emphasis on treating the root cause—agni—
